expectation_evaluation.note: The reviewer inspected the exact execution-snapshot caller and did not emit the disproved shared-lock/upgrade claim. Other surviving findings remain in the output so this receipt does not mistake silence for a generally clean review.

reviewer_output.coverage_note: All 27 changed files were diff-reviewed, and risk-relevant caller, persistence, file-loading, provider, and runtime paths were deep-read at the exact head and compared with base where needed. Contributor code and tests were not executed, as required.

findings.claim: Fleet validation can omit document-derived images for Assistants owned by another tenant user, allowing an incompatible Skill pin to advance.
findings.evidence: organization_skill_service.py:617-630 validates every target through the request-scoped admin AssistantService. assistant_service.py:825-828 expands vision attachments through FileService, but file_service.py:481-495 and file_repo.py:229-245 load derivatives only where Files.user_id equals the current admin. get_by_ids_for_validation hydrates the target owner's parent attachments at assistant_repo.py:807-817, so cross-owner parents are present while their derived images silently disappear. The owner-bound ask path expands those images at assistant_service.py:2234-2243; their image tokens can then make the newly advanced configuration fail the ask-time context guard.
findings.disproof_checks: Confirmed derivative metadata inherits the uploader's user_id at file_service.py:315-330, target discovery includes non-default personal and shared Assistants, and no later fleet validation restores missing derivatives before the write. The added fleet tests use admin-owned or attachment-free Assistants and do not exercise a cross-owner vision document.

findings.claim: Governance saves with unrestricted models now perform a provider lookup per MCP-configured personal default instead of using the batch preload.
findings.evidence: assistant_service.py:917-922 preloads only effective_config.available_models, which policy_resolver.py:115-120 leaves empty when model restriction is disabled. The changed page path at assistant_service.py:970-1024 nevertheless validates every configured-MCP personal default and passes no adapter for its current model. completion_service.py:185-186 then calls _get_adapter for each Assistant, issuing a provider query each time. A 10,000-user tenant can therefore add roughly 10,000 provider reads to one otherwise bounded governance update.
findings.disproof_checks: Compared base: MCP projection and provider-payload preflight were gated by on-demand candidate IDs, so the always-only/configured-MCP path did not make these calls. The batch loader caches providers only within the models supplied to that call. The query-count regression test enables an explicit model restriction, so its model is preloaded and it does not cover the unrestricted/default path.

findings.claim: One target using an inactive provider can abort an entire fleet chunk even when that target needs no provider adapter for fit validation.
findings.evidence: organization_skill_service.py:559-568 unconditionally loads adapters for every target model before processing any target. load_active_litellm_provider rejects an inactive provider at litellm_provider.py:113-129, producing a 503 before per-target outcomes. For an Assistant with only always-on Skills and no MCP servers, the actual fit owner returns before provider preparation at assistant_service.py:630-638, so ordinary save-equivalent validation does not require that provider at all.
findings.disproof_checks: Confirmed providers can be deactivated while attached models remain, completion_model_repo.all(with_deprecated=True) does not filter provider activity, and there is no per-target exception handling around the batch preload. The deprecated-model regression test retains an active provider and therefore does not falsify this path.
